doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Algiers places, ball games and Frankie Duson
title: Old halls still standing across the river: Eureka Hall
summary: Russell asks which old Algiers halls survive so he can photograph them. Martin names Eureka Hall at the Cut-Off and mentions two or three small halls and a school.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Are there any other old halls over there on that side of the river that are still like down at the Cut-Off or any place that you think might still be there? I could try to take a picture of them sometime, it'd be nice to have a picture of them.
The only thing I know is down there that's the... Eureka. Eureka. We got three little halls in there, where they could open the club. There were?
Three of them. What were the names the other, you remember? I forget the name of them.
Eureka Hall down there. I guess if I go down there somebody might tell me around there would know where they are. Well did you guys go back at the school halls back there?

That's me. Eureka. I'm talking about them old halls. Yeah, because I know Bob played back in the school there back there. He played at the school. Yeah. The school that's built there. The school that's built there. I'm speaking about when the halls was down there when Charlie McDowell and them was down there with boys. The Ricker and them. I know the name of them was too hard, but I didn't know.
Well that's all right. You might find they might still be there. Yes.
